Leah to share benchmark harness repo and runbook link
Customer to provide representative scripts and tokenized sample by 2026-04-14

action_items: Leah Kim: Share benchmark harness repo, runbook, and test vectors - due 2026-04-09
Michael Chen: Provide representative inference scripts and dataset samples (anonymized) - due 2026-04-14
Priya Rao: Confirm VPC peering and SSO requirements; share security contact - due 2026-04-10

summary: Kickoff scoping for benchmark-driven POC. Agreed success metrics (p95 latency < 350ms for streaming use case, throughput target 30 req/s for bulk inference, cost target <= $0.0008/token effective). Plan: customer provides scripts and sample workload; Redwood runs harness in hosted + dedicated variants, returns results and recommendations. Timeline: share artifacts by 4/14, smoke run week of 4/20, 2-week focused benchmark after initial tuning.
transcript:
00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Samir from Redwood, and with me is Leah from our infra team. Quick roll call?
00:06 Michael: Michael Chen here, Head of ML at DataHarbor.
00:09 Priya: Priya Rao, SRE.
00:11 Luis: Luis Ortega, product.
00:13 Samir: Great, thanks. We called this POC scoping for benchmark harness integration - want to align on success criteria, what your scripts look like, and streaming vs non-streaming behavior.
00:24 Michael: Yeah, the big thing for us is real-time ingestion and summarization for alerts. So streaming latency matters. We want to see p95 under, like, 300 to 400 ms when streaming. For batch embedding jobs we care more about throughput/cost.
00:39 Leah: Got it. Quick question on your traffic shape
is this a steady stream of small requests or bursty?
00:44 Michael: Mostly bursts. During incidents we get spikes
short windows where 20-50 req/s for a few minutes, otherwise 2-3 req/s. Payload sizes range 200-1200 tokens after context.
00:56 Samir: That's helpful. For benchmarking we'll want representative scripts that mimic that burstiness and the token distribution. Can you share samples?
01:03 Michael: Yep, we have a suite of Python scripts that call our current endpoint. We'll sanitize and share by next week.
01:09 Leah: Perfect. On the harness side we support streaming and non-streaming modes; our harness can replay your script, preserve timing, and measure per-token latency and end-to-end latency. There's a GitHub repo and a runbook I'll send links after this call.
01:22 Luis: When you say streaming, do you mean server-sent events style? We use a websocket-ish streaming client.
01:28 Leah: We support SSE and websocket-style streaming. The key is measuring incremental token latency and flush behavior. For streaming success we'll measure token emission delay, initial token delay, and final completion time.
01:39 Priya: Security question will the hosted runs require VPC peering or will you run in our VPC? We have strict data residency and KMS requirements.
01:47 Samir: For the POC we can run two variants: Redwood-hosted (we'll sign BAA/SLA checks as needed) and a private Dedicated pool behind your VPC. For the hosted run we'll ensure customer data is not persisted; for Dedicated/private we can integrate with your KMS and VPC.
01:58 Michael: Okay, Dedicated seems likely if costs/latency check out. Also we need audit logs and SOC 2 evidence do you have those docs?
02:05 Samir: Yes, we'll share our SOC 2 summary and relevant compliance pack. Leah, note to attach the security deck.
02:09 Leah: Noted, I'll include SOC 2, ISO summary, and details on encryption at rest and KMS key rotation.
02:15 Michael: On metrics let's be explicit. For streaming use case: target p95 token latency < 350 ms, initial token latency < 200 ms, error rate < 0.5%. For batch / embedding use case: throughput 30 req/s with median latency < 600 ms and cost target under $0.0008 per token effective.
02:33 Samir: Sounds reasonable. We'll frame the POC around those success criteria and report p50/p90/p95 and cost/token for each model variant.
02:41 Luis: Do you support quantized models for lower cost? We want to know if you can recommend a quantized workflow without regressing quality.
02:47 Leah: Yes our runtime supports int8/4-bit quantization profiles. Part of the harness runs side-by-side model variants and computes automatic quality regressions using a small eval set you provide.
02:58 Michael: Nice. For quality we can provide a short eval set of ~500 prompts. We want a simple rubric: semantic similarity + business rules pass/fail.
03:07 Samir: That will work. We'll run quality checks and tie them to any cost comparisons.
03:12 Priya: For the Dedicated run, networking we need to confirm egress rules and IP allowlists. We'll share SRE contact.
03:18 Samir: Please send the contact, Leah will coordinate the VPC peering checklist.
03:22 Leah: Quick note on harness integration: we can either run your scripts as-is against our harness or adapt them into our runner wrappers. Running them as-is keeps fidelity but sometimes we need to instrument them to capture token-level timing. We recommend a short adapter layer.
03:36 Michael: We prefer minimal changes. Our ops team is okay adding a small wrapper.
03:40 Leah: Great. We'll provide an adapter example in Python and node.
03:45 Luis: What's the typical timeline? We have a board review late May and want results before then.
03:50 Samir: Timeline we propose: share scripts and samples by 2026-04-14, initial smoke run week of 2026-04-20 (1-2 days), then a 2-week tuning and benchmark period ending early May. Final report and recommendations by 2026-05-08. Is that aligned?
04:06 Michael: That aligns with our milestones.
04:09 Priya: For the smoke run, will you need credentials or just public endpoints?
04:13 Leah: For hosted runs we'll ask for test tokens that can be revoked. For Dedicated we'll coordinate provisioning via your SRE and IR rules.
04:20 Michael: Another question how do you measure cost/token? If you do batching automatically it can change cost profile.
04:25 Samir: We report both raw exec cost and effective cost after batching/kv cache effects. The harness will run with your real request patterns so it captures batching impact. We'll show modeled and observed cost per token.
04:36 Luis: Do you model KV-cache warmups? Our flow often has repeated context where KV cache helps a lot.
04:41 Leah: Yes, harness supports warmup patterns. You can provide sequences that reuse context. We'll measure cold vs warm cache behavior.
04:48 Michael: Great. For metrics we also want p99 numbers sometimes incidents need worst-case numbers rather than p95.
04:53 Samir: We'll include p99 but focus pass/fail on p95 for streaming SLA. Ok Leah, can you talk about the harness outputs and artifacts we'll get?
04:59 Leah: Sure you'll get a CSV and JSON summary with per-request timing, per-token timing, model variant labels, and cost calculations. We'll also attach a dashboard screenshot with throughput over time, heatmaps for token latencies, and a regression report for quality. Also we'll provide raw logs and an annotated trace for a handful of requests.
05:19 Priya: Will those logs contain sensitive input? We need redaction options.
05:23 Leah: We can redact at the token level; the harness supports masking and replacing with hashed placeholders for PII. We'll show how to anonymize the sample data.
05:31 Michael: For orchestration, do you run canary rollouts, or is that outside the POC scope?
05:36 Samir: For POC we'll just demonstrate performance; rollouts are part of Dedicated product features but we can discuss in parallel.
05:42 Luis: What about model fallbacks? If capacity is constrained can you fallback to smaller quantized variant?
05:46 Leah: We support routing policies for fallback. In the benchmark we'll simulate a constrained pool and show how fallback affects latency and cost.
05:54 Michael: On the topic of external competitors, we've looked at Anthropic via their API and also self-hosted via Hugging Face. We want to compare Redwood's latency/cost on similar models.
06:03 Samir: We'll include comparable baselines. If you have specific model IDs you care about include them in the scripts or metadata.
06:09 Michael: We'll include our current model version and a smaller variant for comparison.
06:13 Samir: Good. A few housekeeping things: Leah will share the harness repo link, security pack, and a short POC scope doc. Samir will send pricing and success criteria doc. Customer will send scripts and samples.
06:24 Priya: Also, we'll need SSO/SAML details if you need to provision access for our auditors.
06:28 Samir: We'll follow your SSO onboarding process; we'll send an onboarding checklist.
06:33 Michael: Anything else on streaming vs non-streaming specifics? We have a use case where we call completion with partial-turn updates avg partial chunk size is ~25 tokens every 80 ms. We'd like to see token flush timings.
06:46 Leah: We'll instrument token emission every chunk and report inter-token delay distributions. That will show whether your client-side pacing or server flush policy is the bottleneck.
06:56 Luis: If the harness points to a server-side flush problem, do you typically tune kernel choices or batching window?
07:02 Leah: Both. Our runtime can switch kernels and adjust batching thresholds and KV cache eviction. Part of the POC tuning is kernel selection and compilation flags.
07:12 Michael: Is there anything you need from legal for the hosted runs?
07:15 Samir: We'll need a redacted NDA for the POC and note on permitted data types; I'll include a simple POC agreement template.
07:22 Priya: We'll do that.
07:25 Samir: Final recap: deliverables and owners Leah: harness + runbook + repo link; Samir: pricing + POC doc + SOC2 pack; Michael: scripts + sample dataset; Priya: SRE contact and networking details; Luis: success criteria confirmation on product side. We'll aim for smoke run week of 4/20.
07:45 Michael: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
07:48 Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up with links and next steps.
07:52 [call ends]

Note: transcript contains occasional transcription errors (e.g., "k-v cash" for KV cache in earlier automated transcription, "sock two" for SOC 2 noted in auto notes) and some speaker attribution approximations in a few lines. Links referenced: (1) Benchmark harness repo - https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness (example) (2) POC scope doc & pricing spreadsheet (link to be provided by Samir)
